coverage: Both full English editions, all 12 books and 1,188 paragraphs. Named people, gods, angels, devils, personified powers, named monsters and named peoples. Places, rivers, mountains and constellations are not cast.

entities.name: Satan
entities.body: The rebel archangel, once Lucifer, who leads a third of Heaven into war, is thrown into Hell, and crosses Chaos alone to ruin the new world. Milton gives him the poem’s best speeches and then shows what they cost.

entities.name: God
entities.body: The Father, who foresees the fall, declares that Man fell by his own free will, and accepts the Son’s offer to die for him.

entities.name: The Son
entities.body: The Son of God, who volunteers to become Man and die for him, drives the rebel angels out of Heaven in his chariot, makes the world in six days, and comes down to judge Adam and Eve and clothe them.

entities.name: Adam
entities.body: The first man, made in God’s image and given everything except one tree. He eats knowing exactly what he is doing, because he will not be left without Eve.

entities.name: Eve
entities.body: The first woman, made from Adam’s rib, who wants to work apart from him and meets the serpent alone. She eats first, and she is also the first of the two to ask for forgiveness.

entities.name: Beelzebub
entities.body: Satan’s second, the first to answer him on the burning lake; he puts Satan’s own plan to the council as if it were his own.

entities.name: Moloch
entities.body: The fiercest of the devils, who argues for open war — and, on earth, the horrid king smeared with the blood of children passed through fire in the valley of Hinnom.

entities.name: Belial
entities.body: The devil who counsels ignoble ease in words that sound like reason; on earth, the spirit of the sons of Belial who fill the streets with riot.

entities.name: Mammon
entities.body: The devil who proposes that Hell be mined and made comfortable; the least erected spirit that fell, who kept his eyes on the golden pavement even in Heaven.

entities.name: Mulciber
entities.body: The architect of Pandemonium, thrown out of Heaven and remembered by the Greeks as the smith-god who fell all day and landed on Lemnos.

entities.name: Azazel
entities.body: The tall cherub who unfurls Satan’s standard over the fallen host.

entities.name: Nisroch
entities.body: Chief of the Principalities, who stands up in the rebel assembly to complain that pain has unmanned them.

entities.name: Adramelech
entities.body: A rebel angel beaten down in the war in Heaven.

entities.name: Asmadai
entities.body: A rebel angel overthrown beside Adramelech.

entities.name: Ariel
entities.body: A rebel angel scorched and overthrown by Abdiel on the second day of battle.

entities.name: Arioch
entities.body: A rebel angel overthrown beside Ariel.

entities.name: Ramiel
entities.body: A rebel angel whose violence Abdiel blasted.

entities.name: Asmodeus
entities.body: The demon of the Book of Tobit, driven off by a fish’s smoke; Milton uses him for a spirit less pleased with Eden’s scents than Satan was.

entities.name: Michael
entities.body: The archangel who leads Heaven’s armies on the first day of the war and wounds Satan; afterwards he drives Adam and Eve out of Paradise and shows Adam the future first.

entities.name: Gabriel
entities.body: Chief of the angelic guard at the gate of Paradise, who catches Satan squatting at Eve’s ear and faces him down.

entities.name: Raphael
entities.body: The affable archangel sent to warn Adam; he tells the whole story of the war in Heaven and the Creation over an afternoon meal, and answers Adam’s questions about astronomy and about love.

entities.name: Uriel
entities.body: Regent of the sun and the sharpest-sighted spirit in Heaven, who is nevertheless deceived by Satan disguised as a young cherub — hypocrisy, Milton says, is the one evil that walks invisible.

entities.name: Uzziel
entities.body: Gabriel’s next in power, sent to sweep the south of the garden.

entities.name: Ithuriel
entities.body: One of the two cherubs who find Satan at Eve’s ear and make him resume his own shape with a touch of the spear.

entities.name: Zephon
entities.body: Ithuriel’s companion, who tells Satan to his face that he is no longer recognisable as an angel.

entities.name: Zophiel
entities.body: The swiftest-winged of the cherubim, who brings warning that the rebel host is coming on again.

entities.name: Abdiel
entities.body: The one seraph in Satan’s whole province who refuses him and walks out alone — faithful only he among the faithless — and who strikes the first blow of the war.

entities.name: Sin
entities.body: Satan’s daughter, who sprang fully formed from his head in Heaven, bore him Death, and keeps the key of Hell-gate. Woman to the waist and serpent below, she is both the personage and the thing itself.

entities.name: Death
entities.body: Satan’s son by his own daughter, and her rapist; a shape that is not a shape, black as night and crowned. Milton never lets the reader separate the figure at the gate from the sentence passed on Adam.

entities.name: Chaos
entities.body: The Anarch old, who rules the abyss between Hell and Heaven and cheers Satan on because every new world costs him territory. Milton uses the one word for the ruler and for the region he rules.

entities.name: Night
entities.body: Chaos’s sable-vested consort, eldest of things, whose standard Satan promises to raise again over the new world.

entities.name: Demogorgon
entities.body: A dreaded name among the powers of the abyss, spoken and not explained.

entities.name: Orcus
entities.body: One of the powers standing by the throne of Chaos.

entities.name: Ades
entities.body: One of the powers standing by the throne of Chaos; Hades under an older spelling.

entities.name: Discord
entities.body: Daughter of Sin, who brings death among the animals by setting them against each other.

entities.name: Rumour
entities.body: One of the courtiers of Chaos, named with Chance, Tumult and Confusion.

entities.name: Tumult
entities.body: One of the courtiers of Chaos.

entities.name: Confusion
entities.body: One of the courtiers of Chaos, all of them embroiled together.

entities.name: Chemos
entities.body: The obscene dread of Moab’s sons, worshipped from Aroar to Nebo; Peor was his other name, when he enticed Israel at Sittim.

entities.name: Baalim
entities.body: The general name of the male gods worshipped between the Euphrates and the brook of Egypt — spirits who can take either sex, or both.

entities.name: Ashtaroth
entities.body: The general name of the female gods of the same coast, for whose sake Israel often forsook its living strength.

entities.name: Astoreth
entities.body: Queen of heaven with the crescent horns, called Astarte by the Phoenicians, to whom Sidonian virgins paid their vows by moonlight — and for whom Solomon built a temple.

entities.name: Thammuz
entities.body: The god whose annual wound ran the river of Lebanon purple, and whose Syrian women wailed for him — the idolatry Ezekiel saw in the porch of the Temple.

entities.name: Dagon
entities.body: The sea-monster god of the Philistines, man above and fish below, whose own image fell headlong before the Ark in his own temple.

entities.name: Rimmon
entities.body: The god of Damascus, who lost a leper and won a king in the same day.

entities.name: Osiris
entities.body: The chief of the Egyptian gods, worshipped in brutish forms — and remembered by Milton as the calf the Israelites made in Oreb.

entities.name: Isis
entities.body: One of the Egyptian gods named with Osiris and Orus.

entities.name: Orus
entities.body: One of the Egyptian gods named with Osiris and Isis; Horus under an older spelling.

entities.name: Belus
entities.body: A Babylonian god, named with Serapis for the magnificence Egypt and Assyria built for their idols.

entities.name: Serapis
entities.body: An Egyptian god, named with Belus in the same comparison.

entities.name: Titan
entities.body: Heaven’s first-born, whose birthright his younger brother Saturn seized — the first of the three usurpations Milton uses to make the Greek gods a family of rebels.

entities.name: Saturn
entities.body: The god who took the birthright from Titan and lost it in turn to his own son by Rhea; he fled over the Adriatic to Italy and the Celtic west.

entities.name: Jove
entities.body: The youngest usurper, who drove out his father Saturn and reigned — a god by conquest, which is exactly Milton’s point. Called Jupiter and, in Libya, Ammon.

entities.name: Rhea
entities.body: Saturn’s consort and Jove’s mother.

entities.name: Ops
entities.body: Saturn’s consort under her Latin name, named in Eve’s catalogue of the gods who ruled Olympus before Jove.

entities.name: Javan
entities.body: The son of Japheth, from whose offspring the Ionian gods were held to descend.

entities.name: Bacchus
entities.body: The florid son whom Ammon hid with Amalthea from his stepdame’s eye; his revellers tore Orpheus apart, which is why Milton fears for his own voice.

entities.name: Pan
entities.body: The god of field and grove, whose dance with the Graces and the Hours led on the eternal Spring — a Paradise the real one still beats.

entities.name: Sylvanus
entities.body: A woodland god named with Pan for the bowers that never matched Eve’s.

entities.name: Faunus
entities.body: A woodland spirit named with the nymphs who never haunted Eden’s inner bower.

entities.name: Proserpine
entities.body: The girl gathering flowers in the field of Enna when gloomy Dis gathered her — herself a fairer flower, and the cost of her was all her mother’s pain.

entities.name: Ceres
entities.body: Proserpine’s mother, who sought her through the whole world; Milton uses that search for the price of Eden.

entities.name: Dis
entities.body: The lord of the underworld who carried Proserpine off.

entities.name: Juno
entities.body: The wife on whom Jupiter smiles when he impregnates the clouds that shed May flowers.

entities.name: Neptune
entities.body: The sea god whose grudge, with Juno’s, troubled the Greeks and Aeneas in the older epics Milton means to outdo.

entities.name: Aphrodite
entities.body: Aeneas’s mother, named once when Milton lists the quarrels of the classical epics.

entities.name: Hermes
entities.body: The messenger god, whose charmed pipe put the hundred eyes of Argus to sleep and who brought Pandora to Japhet’s unwiser son; Milton also uses his name for quicksilver.

entities.name: Maia
entities.body: Hermes’s mother; Raphael descends in the likeness of her son.

entities.name: Flora
entities.body: The goddess of flowers, on whom Zephyrus breathes; Adam wakes Eve as gently.

entities.name: Zephyrus
entities.body: The west wind, whose breath on Flora is Milton’s measure of a gentle voice.

entities.name: Pomona
entities.body: The goddess of orchards, whose arbour Eve’s bower resembles, and who fled from Vertumnus.

entities.name: Vertumnus
entities.body: The god who pursued Pomona through every shape he could take.

entities.name: Pales
entities.body: The goddess of pastures, named with Pomona for what Eve most resembled.

entities.name: Diana
entities.body: The huntress goddess, whose train of nymphs Eve resembles at her gardening.

entities.name: Bellona
entities.body: The goddess of war, whose engines storm cities — a small thing, Milton says, beside the artillery of the angels.

entities.name: Urania
entities.body: The Heavenly Muse Milton calls on from the first line, and names only in Book 7 — insisting even then that he means the meaning and not the name. She conversed with eternal Wisdom before the hills were made, which is why she and not one of the nine can tell him what happened in Heaven.

entities.name: The Muses
entities.body: The nine of Olympus, whose haunts Milton still wanders even though his own Muse is not one of them; the one who was Orpheus’s mother could not save him.

entities.name: The Graces
entities.body: Attendants of beauty, knit with the Hours in Pan’s dance and waiting on Eve as on a queen.

entities.name: The Hours
entities.body: The circling Hours who wake the morning and unbar the gates of light.

entities.name: Eurynome
entities.body: With Ophion, the first ruler of Olympus in the older story, driven out by Saturn and Ops; Milton offers her as a rumour of Eve.

entities.name: Ophion
entities.body: The serpent the Greeks say ruled Olympus first — Milton’s hint that they were remembering Satan.

entities.name: Hymen
entities.body: The god of marriage, whose torches were lit for the first weddings Adam sees in his vision of the future.

entities.name: Leucothea
entities.body: The sea goddess of the dawn, who wakes and sheds her dew on the earth.

entities.name: Themis
entities.body: The goddess at whose shrine Deucalion and Pyrrha prayed to restore the human race after the flood.

entities.name: Argus
entities.body: The herdsman covered with eyes, all of which Hermes charmed asleep; the cherubim of the gate have more, and stay awake.

entities.name: Medusa
entities.body: The Gorgon set to guard the ford of Lethe, so that no damned soul can reach the water that would let it forget.

entities.name: Gorgons
entities.body: Named with Hydras and Chimeras among the shapes that haunt the frozen continent of Hell — worse, Milton says, than fables ever invented.

entities.name: Hydras
entities.body: Named with Gorgons and Chimeras in the same catalogue.

entities.name: Chimeras
entities.body: Named last in the same catalogue: Gorgons, and Hydras, and Chimeras dire.

entities.name: The Furies
entities.body: The harpy-footed powers who haul the damned from fire to ice and back; Death stands as fierce as ten of them.

entities.name: Scylla
entities.body: The monster of the strait between Calabria and Sicily, whose hell-hounds Milton says were less abhorred than Sin’s.

entities.name: Charybdis
entities.body: The whirlpool Ulysses steered away from, at the cost of the other side.

entities.name: Typhon
entities.body: One of the giants who warred on Jove, kept in a den near Tarsus; Milton uses him to size Satan.

entities.name: Briareos
entities.body: The hundred-handed giant, named with Typhon in the same measurement.

entities.name: Leviathan
entities.body: The hugest of living creatures, which a night-bound pilot mistakes for an island and moors to — Milton’s last and best image for the size of Satan.

entities.name: Behemoth
entities.body: The biggest of earth-born creatures, heaving himself out of the ground on the sixth day.

entities.name: Python
entities.body: The huge serpent bred out of the mud after the flood, which Satan outgrows in the hall of Pandemonium.

entities.name: Pegasus
entities.body: The winged horse whose flight Milton claims to have passed, and off whose rider he begs not to fall.

entities.name: Bellerophon
entities.body: The rider thrown from the winged horse for aiming too high, who wandered the Aleian field alone — Milton’s warning to himself.

entities.name: Hercules
entities.body: Called Alcides; crowned with conquest, he felt the poisoned robe and threw the man who brought it into the sea.

entities.name: Lichas
entities.body: The messenger Hercules hurled from the top of Oeta into the sea for bringing him the robe.

entities.name: Orpheus
entities.body: The Thracian poet torn apart by Bacchus’s revellers while his Muse-mother could not defend him; Milton, blind and out of favour, asks not to end the same way.

entities.name: Pandora
entities.body: The woman the gods adorned and sent to Japhet’s unwiser son, to the ruin of mankind — a story Milton lays beside Eve’s and does not soften.

entities.name: Japhet
entities.body: The father of the unwiser son who accepted Pandora.

entities.name: Deucalion
entities.body: With Pyrrha, the survivor of the flood who prayed at the shrine of Themis to restore mankind; Adam and Eve praying together are the older pair.

entities.name: Pyrrha
entities.body: Deucalion’s wife, named with him for the same prayer.

entities.name: Circe
entities.body: The enchantress whose beasts came at her call; the animals of Eden came at Eve’s more readily.

entities.name: Cadmus
entities.body: Turned into a serpent in Illyria with Hermione — one of the shapes Milton says was less lovely than the one Satan chose.

entities.name: Hermione
entities.body: Cadmus’s wife, transformed with him.

entities.name: Cham
entities.body: Ham under his old name, whom the Gentiles called Ammon and the Libyans Jove.

entities.name: Amalthea
entities.body: Hidden by Ammon from his wife’s eye, with her son Bacchus, on the Nyseian isle.

entities.name: Achilles
entities.body: The hero whose wrath Milton names as the old epic subject his own exceeds.

entities.name: Turnus
entities.body: The rival whose fury over Lavinia Milton names in the same breath as Achilles’s wrath.

entities.name: Lavinia
entities.body: The bride Turnus lost.

entities.name: Aeneas
entities.body: Aphrodite’s son, whom Neptune and Juno hounded through the older epic.

entities.name: Alcinous
entities.body: The king whose gardens hosted Odysseus, and which Milton says were fabled where Eden was real.

entities.name: Odysseus
entities.body: The guest of Alcinous, and the sailor who shunned Charybdis; Milton names him under both his Greek and Latin names.

entities.name: Tantalus
entities.body: The man from whose lips the water always fled — as the water of Lethe flees the damned.

entities.name: Arthur
entities.body: Uther’s son, girt with British and Armoric knights; Milton names the romances he had once meant to write about and did not.

entities.name: Uther
entities.body: Arthur’s father, named for him.

entities.name: Charlemagne
entities.body: The emperor who fell with all his peerage at Fontarabbia — the last of the romance names Milton lays aside.

entities.name: Thamyris
entities.body: A blind poet of legend, named among the company Milton hopes to join.

entities.name: Maeonides
entities.body: Homer under the name of his supposed birthplace, named among the blind.

entities.name: Tiresias
entities.body: The blind prophet of Thebes, named with Phineus among the blind who saw.

entities.name: Phineus
entities.body: A blind prophet of the Argonaut story, named last in Milton’s list of the blind.

entities.name: Amram
entities.body: Moses’s father; the potent rod of Amram’s son is Milton’s figure for Satan’s spear calling up the fallen host like locusts.

entities.name: Moses
entities.body: The shepherd on Oreb who first taught the chosen how the heavens and earth rose out of Chaos, and one of the two brothers sent to bring Israel out of Egypt.

entities.name: Aaron
entities.body: Moses’s brother, sent with him to Pharaoh; the twelve stones of his breastplate are Milton’s measure for the light of Heaven.

entities.name: Pharaoh
entities.body: The impious king over whose realm the locusts hung like night, and whose army the sea swallowed.

entities.name: Busiris
entities.body: The Egyptian king whom the Red Sea overthrew with his chivalry while he pursued the sojourners of Goshen.

entities.name: Solomon
entities.body: The wisest heart in Israel, led by fraud to build a temple to Astoreth on the hill of scandal; later, the king who enshrined the Ark.

entities.name: Josiah
entities.body: The good king who drove the idols from their shrines and threw them into hell.

entities.name: Eli
entities.body: The priest whose sons turned atheist and filled the house of God with violence.

entities.name: Ezekiel
entities.body: The prophet who was led by vision to see the dark idolatries of alienated Judah in the sacred porch.

entities.name: Samson
entities.body: The champion who rose from the treacherous lap of Delilah shorn of his strength — Milton’s image for Adam and Eve waking after the fall.

entities.name: Delilah
entities.body: The Philistine woman in whose lap Samson lost his hair and his strength.

entities.name: Tobit
entities.body: The blind man of the apocryphal book whose son Raphael travelled with.

entities.name: Tobias
entities.body: Tobit’s son, whose marriage Raphael secured against the demon Asmodeus.

entities.name: Abraham
entities.body: The patriarch who leaves Ur and his gods on nothing but a call, and in whose seed all nations are to be blessed — the first of the figures Michael shows Adam.

entities.name: Isaac
entities.body: Abraham’s son, named in the line that runs down to Joshua.

entities.name: Jacob
entities.body: The grandson who saw the ladder of angels at Luz while fleeing from Esau, and whom the angels met again at Mahanaim.

entities.name: Esau
entities.body: The brother Jacob was fleeing when he dreamed of the ladder.

entities.name: Joshua
entities.body: The commander who leads Israel into Canaan and at whose word the sun stands still over Gibeon; Michael points out that his name is the name of Jesus.

entities.name: David
entities.body: The shepherd king of the royal house from which the Messiah is promised to come.

entities.name: Noah
entities.body: The one just man, who builds the ark and rides out the flood; Michael shows Adam the whole of it.

entities.name: Mary
entities.body: The second Eve, hailed with the same word the angel used to the first; the Virgin Mother of the promised seed.

entities.name: Peter
entities.body: The keeper of the keys at Heaven’s wicket, seen in vision above the Paradise of Fools.

entities.name: John
entities.body: The evangelist who saw the angel standing in the sun.

entities.name: Dominic
entities.body: The founder whose habit the dying put on to be sure of Paradise — a fraud, Milton says, that blows into the Limbo of Vanity with the Franciscan robes.

entities.name: Israel
entities.body: The chosen race, who forsook their living strength for Baalim and Ashtaroth and fell before despicable enemies.

entities.name: The Ammonites
entities.body: Moloch’s worshippers in Rabba and the watery plain.

entities.name: The Phoenicians
entities.body: Who called Astoreth by the name Astarte.

entities.name: The Canaanites
entities.body: The nation Israel skirts on the march out of Egypt, to avoid a war that might frighten them back into slavery.

entities.name: The Chaldeans
entities.body: The people of Ur, whose gods Abraham left behind.

entities.name: The Philistines
entities.body: Dagon’s people, in Gath and Ascalon and Accaron and Gaza.

entities.name: The Gentiles
entities.body: Milton’s word for the nations who kept the fallen angels’ names alive as gods.

entities.name: The Greeks
entities.body: Who honoured Mulciber as their smith-god, and whom Neptune and Juno hounded in the older epic.

entities.name: The Apostles
entities.body: On whom the Spirit was first poured, and who confounded their proudest persecutors.

entities.name: The Americans
entities.body: Whom Columbus found girt with feathers — Milton’s comparison for Adam and Eve in their first clothing.

entities.name: The named winds
entities.body: Milton gives the winds their old names and lets them loose on the world after the fall: Boreas, Caecias, Argestes and Thrascias out of the north, Notus and Afer from the south, Eurus and Zephyr from east and west, with Sirocco and Libecchio. Before the fall, no wind blew hard.

entities.name: Galileo
entities.body: The Tuscan artist with the optic glass, viewing the moon from Fesole — the only living person Milton names in the whole poem, and he names him twice.

entities.name: Empedocles
entities.body: Who leapt into Etna’s flames to be thought a god, and blows about the Limbo of Vanity for it.

entities.name: Cleombrotus
entities.body: Who leapt into the sea to reach the afterlife Plato had described, and ended in the same Limbo.

entities.name: Plato
entities.body: Whose Elysium Cleombrotus drowned himself to reach.

entities.name: Xerxes
entities.body: Who bridged the Hellespont to yoke the freedom of Greece and whipped the sea for breaking it — Milton’s comparison for Sin and Death bridging Chaos.

entities.name: Scipio
entities.body: Rome at its height, born of a woman a god was said to have visited.

entities.name: Olympias
entities.body: Alexander’s mother, visited in the same way; both stories are serpents, which is the point.

entities.name: Columbus
entities.body: Who found the Americans naked and feathered.

entities.name: Montezuma
entities.body: Whose seat at Mexico is one of the kingdoms Michael shows Adam from the hill.

entities.name: Atahualpa
entities.body: Whose richer seat at Cusco is named beside Montezuma’s.

entities.name: Tamerlane
entities.body: Whose throne at Samarkand is another of the empires in Adam’s view.
